subject: How to set the prior for the Berkson Measurement Error model

messages.author: ff1a5632abbf2fe9
messages.subject: How to set the prior for the Berkson Measurement Error model
parts:
Hi, LNLA experts

After reading the paper of 'Measurement error in GLMMs with INLA', I have two question regarding the prior setting for the berkson measurement error model


The relevant code is the following, in which 'prec.u' is the precision for the latent gaussion Berkson error model

prec.u <- 4.98 # estimated value
prec.tau <- 57.83 # estimated value
prior.beta <- c(0,0.0001)
prior.prec.u <- c(100,99/prec.u) # prior mode at prec.u
prior.tau <- c(100,99/prec.tau) # prior mode at prec.tau

1. In the main text, the calculation for 'prec.u' has used the unobservable 'x_ij'. How can we achieve this?

2. For 'prec.u' and 'prec.tau', unlike the non-informative prior, the priors have very small variance. And they heavily concentrated on the mode value, which imposes strong prior information. Is this reasonable? Maybe this question is a general Bayesian question, rather than a specific INLA one. But I would really appreciate if you can give me some brief explanations or references.


Thank you in advance
Xing

messages.author: 059504e415ddf983
messages.subject: Re: How to set the prior for the Berkson Measurement Error model
parts:
Dear Xing,

thank you for your comments. They refer to an old version of our paper. We have reconsidered our prior choice in a revised version of the manuscript where you will also find a motivation for the different priors (see attachement).

Best regards,
Andrea
